items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: Andy Williams called me because he had somebody in New York -- or Chicago -- that couldn't play his music

ctx.x: Well, I've always had a thing -- I always wanted to end up on top of anything I'd do; I want to remember being at the top. I don't want someone -- I didn't want anyone to remember me later on, saying, in '77, say, you really should have heard him play in '54 or '55. Because I had lived with that all of my life; I'd always told my wife and my son that I would not be sitting up on the bandstand like Zooty, Zooty, for instance -- you know, Zooty played until he was in the seventies.

That's admirable, but to me, it's kind of pitiful, too; I know that's the man's life, but I think that a man is put here to do more than one thing, you know, and I never thought of myself as being one dimensional, and I believe that I can learn to do anything, and when I came off the road, I went to -- Andy Williams called me because he had somebody in New York -- or Chicago -- that couldn't play his music, and he must have called me 7 or 8 times, because I didn't want to play any more.
And so he made me a proposition I could not refuse, and so I went and I stayed for 3 weeks, and I came back in '62 -- and that was the last time that I played.
